name: TEKEX #10
addr: The Embassy, JE2 4WG Saint Helier, Saint Helier
summary: Welcome to TEKEX #10. This month we will be bringing 2 very compelling speakers to the group. John Morris and Julian Box.
long:
In a TEKEX first we are lucky enough to have a guest speaker from the UK, John Morris from Smith and Williamson. John leads Smith & Williamson’s Scale-Up programme: an integrated suite of solutions, expertise and support, designed to help businesses scale quickly. With 15 years experience providing strategy and consulting advice to a variety of businesses in a diverse range of sectors this proves to be a compelling talk. We thank Smith and Williamson Jersey for helping organise this speaker.
Secondly, we will be hearing from Julian Box, CEO of Calligo and founder of Vybbe. Julian will be talking to us about his latest global tech enterprise Vybbe...we'll not give anymore away on that.
Thirdly, and in another TEKEX first we will be having a live on screen presentation from Andy Prow, (yes Ed's brother) on his cyber security business www.redshield.co and his rise to businesses success and his funding round.
We are still awaiting to hear if we'll be hosting a third speaker, so watch this space.
Whilst we have a larger space tickets will be limited.

name: TEKEX 11
addr: The Embassy, JE2 4WG Saint Helier, Saint Helier
summary: Welcome to our summer TEKEX #11, where we have a rather topical environmental tech theme.
long:
SPEAKERS
Genevieve Leveille: "Digitalisation of the agricultural value chain" - www.agriledger.io
Genevieve is the Principal Founder of AgriLedger, a FinTech venture aiming to empower agricultural producers by democratizing their access to financial services and improving the transparency of the supply chain.
Marc Laine: ESI Monitor - www.ESImonitor.org
The Environmental and Social Impact Monitor is a not for profit entity, rating businesses for their environmental and social commitments.
"We believe that the Channel Islands can be an example to the world, where a social or environmental award from the ESI Monitor will provide rated businesses with advantage and recognition for their positive action, benefit the local community, reduce our island's impact on the planet and provide local stakeholders and the community the means to exercise positive choices based on the rated commitments of those businesses."

They spotted a gap in the Jersey market and are going for it...however their business will not stop in Jersey, they have much bigger pans to expand.

name: TEKEX #16 - Durrell / Sustainability Benchmarking / MyPay / Virtual Stadium
summary: TEKEX #16 presents 3 top speakers of scaling tech businesses - ESI Monitor / Virtex Stadiums / MyPay and our charity this month - Durrell
long:
We are delighted to be hosting another virtual TEKEX and the last of the summer...let's face it we need some more time off! Despite being the last it is by no means the least, with  an eclectic and energetic line up.
We'll be hearing from Beth Gallichan, Fundraising Manager at Durrell about Reconnecting with nature at Jersey Zoo. "The rapid spread of coronavirus is thought to have started in wildlife markets and has demonstrated how connected we all are. Restoring the health of our planet requires people to positively change how they value the environment. Delve into Durrell’s positive and bold vision for conservation and the vital role of Jersey Zoo."
Please note all tickets are free but we'd be delighted if you could make a donation: https://www.durrell.org/wildlife/product/donation/
There is a neat segway from Durrell to ESI Monitor who are collaborating as we speak. If you do not remember ESI Monitor and Marc Laine / Fred Betley from TEKEX #11 then get ready to hear about  a powerful digital platform that has some fantastic developments.
Next up: Virtex Stadium: The Next-Generation Entertainment Platform...  Tim McGuinness is seeking to build a VR/AR/XR events platform that steps past traditional 2D video broadcast and into three-dimensional virtual content formats.  Simultaneously, Virtex Stadium is giving producers and events organisers everything they know and love from real world venues. As you can imagine these guys are poised for real growth as our world has been turned upside down of late but this start-up does not need a pandemic for success. Listen to the young, bright Tim Mcguinness speak about his journey.
Steve Lavington, Sales Director of MyPay:  Taking on the payment disruptors E-commerce post COVID,  how MyPay are reacting to the challenges and evolving the payments landscape.

name: TEKEX #17
summary: In the next of our virtual series we have the absolute pleasure of listening to 3 main speakers and our local charity, read below...
long:
As always we will have 5 minutes from a local Charity to expose to our audience what they're up to. This month we have a very unique charity that impacts our local female entrepreneurs as well as a global audience. International Womens Academy. We'll hear from Peter Le Masurier and Rachel Hayden. 'Image : Connect : Empower: The worlds first incubator app for student creativity
Next up we will receive the talk that Tim McGuinness was meant to give for TEKEX #16! Virtex Stadiums  are building a fully interactive virtual stadium, built for presenting next-generation entertainment formats and creating a unique viewing experience that bridges the gap between online broadcast and real world events.
We will then hear from Ben Lewis and Callum of Infstream. Much like Tim, Ben represents the definition of young digital entrepreneurialism in Jersey.
Title: "Infstream: Subscription platform for video creators"  https://infstream.com
Finally the enigmatic Harry Boxall, many of whom you may know from Jersey will be talking to us about his scaling business Safelink and their next growth.

name: TEKEX #19
summary: TEKEX #19 is our first 2021 event and I hope marks the last virtual one. We are showcasing some Channel Island and off island businesses.
long:
1) Introduction and update from Ben Lewis on rebranded Flaze - formally Infrstream - www.flaze.com
2) "Finding better products when shopping online – for people and the planet"
David Henry // JoinBeagle.com
73% of people want to shop more sustainably, but they struggle to find better products and to make lasting changes to their routines. We’ve launched a tool to provide recommendations for more sustainable products and services when it matters, when people are browsing online.
3) "How well does your organisation murmurate?"
Perrin Carey // www.govindicia.com
The beauty of starlings murmurating is spell-binding, their unity, synchronicity and collective behaviour is truly magnificent. Each decision made, communicated, implemented, with a simple set of values, with a singularity of purpose; all acting as one.
What if organisations could be like that? Clear on purpose and meaning, defined by key powerful values, which are lived by everyone every day. Where decision-making is transparent, founded on valid information and implemented clearly. Where people are rewarded for challenge and openness, as well as failure. It’s possible, you just have to begin.
Governance is simply how well the humans within your organisation murmurate collectively. GOVindicia™ uses evidence-based practice, interdisciplinary research methodologies and governance expertise, to measure and enhance organisational performance as well as ensure better compliance outcomes.
4) Joel Mills - Offshore Similuators and Jersey's Digital Twin - www.osc.no
OSC SANDBOX
An integrated product of Planning tool, 4D Record playback, Digital twin, AR analysis and Prediction tool.
ed@tekex.co for speaking opportunities.

"Crowdcube: The evolution of equity crowdfunding."
Crowdcube is the world's largest equity crowdfunding platform.
Since Crowdcube was founded in 2011, we have helped more than 1,300 raises successfully fundraise. Simon Franc is the CEO of Anatomap, a UKAS accredited technology company, focused on building apps which empower victims, enhance evidence, boost conviction rates and increase public confidence.
As well as being the Founder of Anatomap, Simon is also the CEO of Forensic Equity, a leading independent Forensic Science Service Provider.

With a potent and incredibly relevant product, some of Jersey's best in industry digital  technologists and a refreshingly candid and open attitude to doing business, this shapes up to be an exciting talk.
John Lee, CEO AMD Nano
Our story and our current raise.
Advanced Material Development (AMD) is a leader in the field of cutting-edge Materials Science. It specialises in funding research into 2D nanotechnologies and materials in collaboration with university partners to develop and commercialise unique solutions for industrial applications. In partnership with customers, it builds deep and lasting relationships that seek to bring solutions to market through various licensing initiatives.
AMD works with leading scientists in world-class laboratory and development facilities. Furthermore, it has identified and is already working with commercial partners to explore the use of these technologies in real-world applications.

A Curative School will have a direct, positive impact on both the academic achievement, ways of learning and mental health.

addr: Les Banques, GY1 3DA Guernsey, Guernsey
summary: TEKEX 3 will be one not to miss...
long:
C﻿heck out our Stellar line-up:
Aaron Chatterley - Indu
Aaron co-Founded beauty retailer feelunique in 2005. He led a partial sale of the business to Private Equity in 2012, and in September 2021 sold the company to LVMH/Sephora.
Aaron is currently launching a new teen beauty brand called indu. He is also an independent Director of Nasdaq listed beauty acquisition company Waldencast, a non-Executive Director of Digital Jersey and an Ambassador for the Prince’s Trust Women Supporting Women.
He was voted one of the 50 most powerful people in Online Retail for 2014 by Retail Week, IoD Director of the Year for a Large Organisation 2013 and finalist in the UK Ernst & Young Entrepreneur of the Year 2012.
Dan Armsden - Crewdentials
“Streamline credential management with Crewdentials, the innovative software platform launched in Guernsey in 2020 by an experienced team of maritime, legal, and tech specialists. Crewdentials provides a user-friendly solution that simplifies onboarding and compliance for both crew and businesses.”
L﻿ouis Pike - Iso-Pass
Louis is the recent Youngpreneur prize winner from the 2022 Guernsey Venture Challenge which saw him winning £5,000 investment towards his on-demand Gym-pass business model. On the night it was suggested that he should look to pivot the idea to more market places and diversify away from just the fitness industry following an aggregator model. This presentation involves Louis’s entrepreneur journey and professional career to date, his experience on the venture capital challenge and the next stage of his journey to re-branding the business and working on a more expansive model to take to market. In addition to his entrepreneur success Louis also works full time as a Senior Associate within PwC’s advisory practice and is studying towards his ACCA qualification.”
M﻿ark Costello - Hubb Insure
Mark Costello started his insurance life as a graduate trainee at RSA before holding senior roles in some of the UK’s largest insurance broking house as well as at some regional brokers. Most of his career has been spent in Sales and marketing leadership roles and in product and distribution design roles. In 2019, frustrated by increasing commissions and reducing service Mark and his co-founders founded hubb. hubb aims to reinvent insurance broking to benefit the customer rather than the broker and is disrupting the global broking market by aligning price with usage through advanced technology, reducing the administrative burden on clients and staff while delivering radical transparency via its ground-breaking open back-office. Through a first-of-its-kind approach that foregrounds AI, automation, and data science, hubb is able to deliver usage-based broking that is 20-30% cheaper than competing incumbents.

🌱 Introducing TEKEX Gen – our first step in building the next generation of innovators.
On 15th September, 5–8pm at PwC, we’re hosting our inaugural TEKEX Gen event.It’s designed specifically for 16–24 year olds who want to explore what innovation means to them, their role in shaping the future, and how they can connect with like-minded peers.
We’ll be joined by some of Jersey’s most influential business leaders who will share their stories, challenges, and advice, designed to inspire and spark fresh thinking.
But more importantly, TEKEX Gen isn’t just about listening. It’s about creating a space where young minds can come together, share ideas, and begin building the future they want to see.
💡 Why TEKEX Gen?Because TEKEX doesn’t just need capital and connections. It needs beautiful minds. The vision is that, over time, we’ll bring together TEKEX and TEKEX Gen audiences, blending experience with fresh perspectives to create even more powerful innovation.
👉 If you are 16–24, or if you have a son or daughter who’d love to be part of this journey, please join us.
📅 TEKEX Gen🗓 15th September🕔 5–8pm📍 PwC, Jersey
Let’s build the future, together.

name: TEKEX - Innovation Breakfast
addr: 10-12 Victoria Street, IM1 2LH Douglas, Douglas
summary: Friendly panel debate to discuss and debate innovation for the Isle of Man - past/present/future.”
long:
Panel friendly debate to discuss and debate innovation for the Isle of Man - past/present/future.
Thank you to our sponsors of the Breakfast - StreamOn Ltd
Thank you to our hosts Mann Benham.
Thank you to James Kingston - CDOT Future for facilitating.
Thank you to our dedicated partners - Rathbones / BDO / C5 / Yoono
The Isle of Man is preparing for a General Election in September 2026. With global technology changing rapidly and with a changing domestic economy, how can the Island best embrace the future?
The event will explore the opportunities and the challenges that face the Isle of Man, and consider how MHKs and the government can embrace the Manx future. We will discuss the Isle of Man in a competitive international context, and discuss what industries and specialisms the IOM should adopt & pursue in the years ahead - opportunities like greentech, crypto, data asset foundations, and AI IP regulations. We will also discuss how best to adopt current and future AI technologies. This is an opportunity for members of the business and professional services community to explore the years ahead, and to engage with aspiring MHKs.
Objectives:
Get aspiring Members of the House of Keys enthused
Showcase to the aspiring MHKs that there are votes to be had via a pro tech agenda.
Explore what industries and specialisms the IOM should adopt/ pursue in the years ahead (for instance, greentech, crypto, the data asset foundations, AI IP experimentation)
Point to the challenges that the IOM faces - declining tax base, coming automation of clerical jobs, reliance of the Island on employment income is threatened by automation
Surface topics of interest to business community + MHKs
Relationship to TEKEX: The event will be associated with but formally separate from the previous event
Content: panel style discussion. Pannellists to give quick 5 min intro into whatever their specialism is, then a guided conversation moderated by James K, with networking afterwards. TOpics
Where are we now, and where will we be? Looks at IOM as it stands, and in comparison to UK and to the other offshore jurisdiction
Horizon scanning: what are the industries of the future
An outline of the IOM economy: highlight to people the issues
The AI opportunity
The Crypto opportunity
The adoption opportunities
